intro.text: A great war of the past. It began when Kalad started it, which drove the old royal family out of Hallandren and into Idris, and it ended generations ago when Peacegiver brought it to a close.
A war of the past, fought over the dyes of the Tears of Edgli and over Breath during a golden age of Awakening. Kalad started it, the royal family fled to Idris, and Peacegiver ended it.

A war fought on Nalthis about three hundred years ago between Hanald, as Hallandren was then called, and the nations of Gys, Huth, Kuth, Pahn Kahl and Tedradel, over the Tears of Edgli and over Breath.

A war fought on Nalthis about three hundred years ago between Hanald, as Hallandren was then called, and Gys, Huth, Kuth, Pahn Kahl and Tedradel. Vasher, as Kalad, started it and, as Peacegiver, ended it.

items.text: The Tears of Edgli made Hanald rich: their bright dyes were prized across Nalthis, yet the flowers grew nowhere but in Hanald's climate, so neighboring nations envied that trade and wanted to seize Hanald for it.
Hoid tells Siri that the war was fought over Breath as well, not only over the Tears, as most people believe.

Lifeless could already be made before the war, but the known Commands cost fifty Breaths for each one, so big Lifeless armies were too expensive. Then a Command was found that made a Lifeless from a single Breath, and ichor-alcohol came into use.

With cheap Lifeless that needed no food or pay and felt no fear or pain, rulers could double their armies. The Manywar became the first war on Nalthis to use Lifeless in great numbers, and Awakened ropes even hurled boulders like siege engines.

New Commands were being found quickly in a golden age of Awakening, much of it the work of the Five Scholars. Hanald's ruling family, the House of Idris, took a keen interest and gathered strong Awakeners and Lifeless.
A vision of war seen by one of the Returned sparked the conflict, prompting a strike against the other nations before they could attack.
Kalad raised a huge army and the royal family split from him and fled T'Telir. Kalad also made a stronger kind of Lifeless that came to be called Kalad's Phantoms.
Once the war began, the Five Scholars went their separate ways, so each side gained Awakening knowledge and methods the others lacked.

During the war, Vasher and Shashara worked together to make Nightblood, a sentient sword given a Command to destroy evil. As a sword it could not tell good from evil, and it caused terrible destruction.
The Manywar's final battle was fought at Twilight Falls. The Pahn Unity, the alliance of nations fighting Hanald, lost its leader there.
Shashara wanted to share with all of Nalthis how to make weapons like Nightblood. Vasher believed such weapons must not spread, and after they argued he killed her with Nightblood.
Hoid tells Siri that Peacegiver dispelled Kalad's Phantoms, brought the war to an end and passed his Breath on to the God King who followed.
Peacegiver gave up some fifty thousand Breaths gathered in the war, placing them in a priest and telling him to keep them safe in case they were ever needed. That priest became the first God King.

Sick of war, Vasher pulled his Phantoms back to Hallandren and took control of his own nation. The threat of his armies scared the other nations into peace. The Hallandren, who could not see why he stopped, named him Peacegiver.
He then Commanded the Phantoms to stand still like statues, as a gift to the city.

For reasons no one now knows, the House of Idris fled T'Telir for Hanald's northern highlands, taking Austrism with them, and founded the kingdom of Idris. They turned away from Awakening and used Austrism to paint it as immoral.
After the royal family left, the Cult of the Returned took over and named the new nation Hallandren. Pahn Kahl was absorbed into it as a province but kept its own religion and culture.

Idris and Hallandren have kept an uneasy peace for three hundred years. The Idrian royals carry the blood of the First Returned and so have a claim to the throne in T'Telir, while Hallandren still sees Idris as a rebel province and resents its mountain-pass tariffs.
About twenty years ago, King Dedelin of Idris agreed a treaty promising a daughter as the God King's bride, hoping to stave off war.
Kalad's Phantoms turn out to be the D'Denir statues of T'Telir, made of Awakened human bones encased in stone.

Over time the Phantoms were forgotten, and the D'Denir came to be seen as Peacegiver's gift, honoring the many thousands who died in the war and a reminder not to go to war. The monstrous Phantoms lived on only as a myth.
Old tensions never fully faded. Tedradel still hates Hallandren, and Pahn Kahl, wanting its independence back, plots to set Idris and Hallandren at war with each other.
